title: Luxury Kitchen Remodel
scope: Custom cabinetry, natural-stone slabs, integrated luxury appliances, islands and prep zones, and coastal-durable finishes for Florida waterfront homes.
trades: Cabinetry, plumbing and electrical, stone fabrication, and finish carpentry under one principal-led schedule.
brands: Sub-Zero, Wolf, Miele, quartzite and marble, custom millwork
cost_table:
TierInvestment RangeWhat's Included
Standard$75,000–$125,000 (per project)Semi-custom cabinetry, quartz counters, mid-tier appliance package, updated lighting and standard layout
Premium$125,000–$250,000 (per project)Full-custom cabinetry, natural stone/quartzite, pro-grade appliances, island reconfiguration, upgraded plumbing/electrical
High-end$250,000–$500,000+ (per project)Imported cabinetry, book-matched slabs, Sub-Zero/Wolf/Miele suite, structural changes, integrated smart-home and hurricane-rated openings

Where the investment goes: Labor & installation 40–55% · Materials 30–45% · Engineering, permits & mgmt 10–20%.
cost_drivers: South Florida luxury kitchen costs are driven mostly by cabinetry grade, stone selection, and appliance packages, which can swing a budget by six figures alone. Coastal permitting, hurricane-rated windows/doors near the kitchen, and older concrete-block or high-rise buildings add cost when moving plumbing, gas, or load-bearing walls. HOA/condo association requirements, elevator-only material access in waterfront towers, and skilled-labor demand in Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach further push pricing above national averages.
faq:
How much does a luxury kitchen remodel cost in South Florida?

Most luxury kitchen remodels run $75,000 to $250,000, with high-end custom projects exceeding $500,000 depending on cabinetry, stone, appliances, and structural work.

Do I need permits for a kitchen remodel in Miami or Fort Lauderdale?

Yes—any plumbing, electrical, gas, or wall changes require permits, and condo/HOA approval is common in waterfront buildings. Cosmetic-only swaps may not, but we recommend permitting for resale and insurance protection.

Why are luxury kitchens more expensive in high-rise condos?

Elevator-only material access, association work-hour rules, sound/water-proofing requirements, and rerouting plumbing within concrete slabs all add labor and coordination costs that single-family homes don't face.

title: Luxury Bathroom Remodel
scope: Primary-suite and spa baths, wet rooms, natural stone, curbless showers, freestanding tubs, and moisture-engineered waterproofing for coastal humidity.
trades: Waterproofing, tile and stone, plumbing, and finish work under one schedule.
brands: Waterworks, THG, natural stone, Schluter systems
cost_table:
TierInvestment RangeWhat's Included
Standard$35,000–$65,000 (per project)Full gut of a standard master bath, porcelain tile, quartz vanity tops, semi-custom cabinetry, frameless glass shower, mid-tier fixtures
Premium$65,000–$120,000 (per project)Large-format porcelain or natural stone, custom vanities, freestanding soaking tub, curbless shower, heated floors, designer fixtures, upgraded lighting
High-end$120,000–$300,000+ (per project)Book-matched marble slabs, full-height stone walls, steam shower, smart-home controls, custom millwork, imported fittings, structural reconfiguration

Where the investment goes: Labor & installation 45–55% · Materials 35–45% · Engineering, permits & mgmt 10–15%.
cost_drivers: In South Florida, luxury bathroom cost is driven mostly by finish level and skilled labor — natural stone slabs, waterproofing to code, and specialty trades (glass, tile setters, plumbers) command premium rates in coastal markets like Miami, Fort Lauderdale, and Palm Beach. High-rise condo projects add cost via HOA approvals, elevator/loading logistics, restricted work hours, and stricter plumbing/waterproofing requirements above occupied units. Permitting timelines, mold/moisture remediation on older waterfront homes, and imported material lead times can also inflate budgets.
faq:
Why do luxury bathroom remodels cost more in South Florida condos?

High-rise and coastal condos add costs through HOA review, insurance/COI requirements, freight elevator scheduling, limited work hours, and stringent waterproofing since any leak affects units below. These logistical constraints can add 15–30% versus a comparable single-family home remodel.

Do I need a permit for a luxury bathroom remodel?

Yes. Any project touching plumbing, electrical, or structural elements requires permits in Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach counties. Moving walls, relocating fixtures, or adding steam showers triggers additional inspections; expect permitting and management to run roughly 10–15% of the total budget.

What single upgrade adds the most cost?

Natural stone — especially book-matched marble slabs and full-height stone walls — is the biggest cost driver, followed by structural reconfiguration and steam/spa systems. Material alone can double a mid-tier budget, and stone fabrication and setting require premium specialty labor.

title: Hotel PIP Renovation
scope: Guestroom and public-space PIPs, soft-goods and case-goods, corridors, and FF&E — phased to keep the hotel open, on-brand, and on schedule.
trades: Phased construction, FF&E procurement/install, MEP, and brand-standard compliance.
brands: Marriott, Hilton, IHG, Hyatt, Wyndham standards
cost_table:
TierInvestment RangeWhat's Included
Standard$15,000–$30,000 per keyBrand-mandated soft goods refresh: FF&E, paint, carpet/LVT, lighting, bath fixtures, case goods
Premium$30,000–$60,000 per keyFull case goods + soft goods, bathroom gut/tile, HVAC upgrades, corridors, lobby/amenity refresh
High-end$60,000–$120,000+ per keyDown-to-studs guestroom rebuild, luxury-brand finishes, structural/MEP overhaul, new amenities, resort spaces

Where the investment goes: Labor & installation 40–55% · Materials 30–45% · Engineering, permits & mgmt 10–20%.
cost_drivers: PIP timelines are brand-dictated and often compressed, forcing phased/occupied renovations that raise labor costs and require night/weekend work in South Florida. Coastal properties face wind-load code upgrades (impact windows/doors), stringent Miami-Dade/Broward permitting, and hurricane-driven material lead times. Brand-standard FF&E specs, older-building surprises (asbestos, outdated MEP, ADA), and high regional labor demand all push budgets up.
faq:
What is a hotel PIP and why does it drive renovation cost?

A Property Improvement Plan is the brand's (Marriott, Hilton, Hyatt, IHG, etc.) mandatory list of upgrades tied to franchise/management agreements. Because scope and finish specs are dictated by the brand rather than owner preference, costs are largely fixed by their standards and completion deadlines, leaving limited room to value-engineer.

Can we stay open during the PIP renovation?

Most South Florida PIPs are done occupied, floor-by-floor or wing-by-wing, to protect revenue. This is doable but adds 10–20% for phasing, dust/noise controls, guest-safety measures, off-hours labor, and longer overall schedules versus a full closure.

How long does a typical hotel PIP take in South Florida?

A soft-goods refresh runs roughly 3–6 months; a full case-goods and bathroom PIP on a mid-size property typically takes 8–14 months including design, brand approvals, and permitting. Miami-Dade/Broward permit review, impact-window lead times, and long-lead FF&E are the most common schedule risks.

What unexpected costs come up on older coastal hotels?

Common surprises include asbestos/lead abatement, outdated plumbing and electrical that must be brought to current code, concrete restoration/spalling from salt exposure, ADA compliance upgrades, and wind-load requirements for windows and doors. Budgeting a 10–15% contingency is strongly advised.

title: Hotel Brand Conversion
intent: hotel brand conversion and re-flag renovation
scope: Full de-flag/re-flag: exterior, signage, lobby, brand amenities, and guestrooms executed to franchisor PIP with hard deadline management.
trades: Brand-critical sequencing, life-safety, signage, and FF&E under one schedule.
brands: Marriott, Hilton, IHG, Hyatt, Wyndham conversions
cost_table:
TierInvestment RangeWhat's Included
Standard$25,000–$45,000 per key (soft-brand / limited-service PIP)Cosmetic refresh: paint, carpet/LVT, case goods, soft goods, signage, brand-standard FF&E, basic lobby update to meet franchise PIP
Premium$45,000–$85,000 per key (full-service re-flag)Guest room gut-refresh, corridors, expanded amenity/F&B, upgraded MEP touchpoints, ADA remediation, exterior refresh, new brand signage package
High-end$85,000–$180,000+ per key (upscale/luxury conversion)Full interior/exterior transformation, structural/MEP overhaul, resort amenities, spa/pool, life-safety upgrades, hurricane-code envelope, premium brand FF&E

Where the investment goes: Labor & installation 40–55% · Materials 30–45% · Engineering, permits & mgmt 10–20%.
cost_drivers: Franchise PIP (Property Improvement Plan) scope is the single biggest cost driver — the incoming brand dictates finishes, FF&E specs, and life-safety upgrades that can force work well beyond a cosmetic refresh. South Florida code triggers add cost: current Florida Building Code wind-load/impact-glass requirements, ADA remediation, fire sprinkler/alarm updates, and coastal corrosion-resistant materials often surface once permits are pulled. Occupied-hotel phasing (keeping revenue floors open), tight downtown/beachfront staging, and hurricane-season scheduling all compress timelines and raise labor premiums.
faq:
What is a PIP and why does it drive my conversion cost?

A Property Improvement Plan is the punch list the incoming brand (Marriott, Hilton, Hyatt, IHG, etc.) requires before you can fly their flag. It ranges from a light soft-goods refresh to a full gut renovation, and it dictates specific FF&E, finishes, technology, and life-safety standards — so two identical-looking hotels can have wildly different per-key costs depending on the brand and tier.

Can I keep the hotel open during a re-flag?

Usually yes, and most owners do to protect cash flow. We phase the work floor-by-floor or wing-by-wing, but occupied-hotel renovation adds 10–20% versus a full closure due to noise/dust controls, off-hours labor, security separation, and slower material staging. We build a phasing plan that balances downtime against schedule cost.

What hidden South Florida costs surprise owners most?

The big three are hurricane-code envelope upgrades (impact glazing, roof attachment), ADA remediation once you touch guest paths and bathrooms, and fire/life-safety system updates triggered by the permit. Older coastal buildings also hide corrosion, concrete spalling, and outdated MEP — we recommend a pre-purchase or pre-PIP condition assessment so these don't blow the budget mid-project.
